reviews.title: It's gotten worse
reviews.text:
When this first came out, it was great. I'm in the Houston area. 

1) I could pick and choose areas (by moving the pin) depending where I'll be and when. 
This is no longer as simple as that. It appears, I need to inout an address or place. 

2) notifications are a joke. HEB & Whole Foods go quickly (marked fave) I never get a notification during the day (it releases the same time each night). 

BUT the dumb app wants to tell me Circle K is available. I don't care about gas station foods. Sorry. It's not even marked as a Favorite. 

So it's harder to find new places (in different areas!) and it doesn’t tell you when your preferred places have more to grab. 

TGTG is a joke now. No one is driving the wheel.

reviews.title: Unfair to its users.
reviews.text:
I have used this service quite a few times to pick up food. 
On the one occasion I was 5 minutes late as normally their pickup time is 08:00 - 09:00 on a weekday but it’s 07:00 - 08:00 on a weekend. I used it for the first time on the weekend and made the mistake of arriving at 08:05, so 5 minutes late. My food was there, I’d been charged for it, but was told I wasn’t allowed it. I message Too Good To Go and you get a chat bot that is utterly useless. This is unfair on its consumers as I have paid for my food, but not collected it. To have such a short pickup window is also unfair. Then to not be able to speak to anyone about your concerns and just get told, oh well nothing we can do. Terrible customer service. People are people and make general mistakes. I would have walked in the store 5 minutes earlier. The concept is good, but the food still went to waste as I wasn’t allowed to collect my order. So you make money, great for you, but the food goes in the bin still. That is then pointless and defeats the purpose of saving food waste. . .

reviews.title: Can’t get anything
reviews.text: I get a notification and within seconds of clicking it, they’re sold out. People are obviously sitting there all day refreshing the page. Should limit how often people are allowed to get the one bag from one vendor each day so others can try the concept maybe.

reviews.title: No dietary specification and late notice
reviews.text: The App is good, no friction regarding my experience on the App. But I’m very disappointed that we can’t pick dietary options (vegetarian, gluten-free..). I’m vegetarian and I picked up a bag from a bakery, only to know later that a chicken roll was included in the bag, isn’t the point of this app to avoid wasting food? I had to go back and give it back to the shop (they kindly switched the roll to a vegetarian one but they complained and said it’d be the first and last time they do this). Also, why and how can the collection time change 5mns prior to the pick up?? The intial time I booked was 5:30, I went there at 5:15, and then a 5:25 I received an email saying the collection time had changed to 5:45.

reviews.title: Threatened/Perplexed
reviews.text: Hey! I'm an app developer, myself, who also created this business to raise funds for my child on the side. I signed up, got perplexed by a tax ID question because I have a Texas Cottage Bakery, and then final exams came up. I received a text message from someone saying they were going to delete my account because they can't get hold of me. I've never had someone threaten that before and it feels hostile. Not all owners want to talk on the phone nor do we like constant sales calls. Some of us have disabilities so we will get to finishing the sign up when we get to it. I mean, unless you have a certain amount of slots per user on your side that you're paying for if you're vibe-coding, I get it, but we don't know that. Guess I'll have to either stick to advertising on my site that I'm selling things for less at the end of the week myself, or, is there another app, or, maybe I should make an app like this, myself? You advertise promoting positivity; DO BETTER. Calling me from a NYC number and then threatening my is not the way the rest of America works. Nope. Toxic.

reviews.title: Love The Concept, But…
reviews.text: I truly love this concept and I adore how affordable the bags are. The process is easy, the instructions are clear, and overall it’s a wonderful app. The only downside is that if you have food restrictions, for example I can’t digest any sort of red meat, you can’t filter that out of the bags. It is truly a surprise bag, and although that is part of the mystery/thrill it prevents me from actually buying a bag because I’m certainly not about to waste my money and gas on something that I can barely touch. Therefore the inclusivity of the app is greatly diminished, and for me, personally, the appeal takes a sharp nosedive. I want to buy these bags, save something from needless waste, but I can’t buy most of the bags because I have no clue if it’s going to contain something I can digest. There has to be some sort of feature where you can filter out bags that do not cater towards your dietary needs if this app wants to truly be great. The excuse that it’s part of the mystery is a lazy one and honestly disappointing, it makes one feel like their needs aren’t taken seriously or that it isn’t something worth caring about. I would love to use this app, I just wish it didn’t feel like I was gambling over whether I could even touch the food or not for every bag I would like to buy.

reviews.title: “Past its peak” can mean rotten and slimy trash
reviews.text:
I saw this trending on social media and thought I’d give it a try when I went to Wholefoods and saw the floral bags. The bouquets were in a paper bag and from the top that you could see some flowers looked great and others were starting to wilt but it looked like out of the 2 bouquets you could make one.

I purchased the deal but when I got home, took the flowers out of the bag, and took the plastic the bouquets come wrapped in off I discovered completely rotted and slimy stems. There was really no way to salvage these flowers and put them in a vase. Out of 2 full bouquets of over 40 flowers and foliage I was able to save 4 flowers and 1 foliage stem. Some still not in the best shape but I tried and they are also wilting quickly.

Customer service was horrible too. They said I don’t “qualify” for a refund only a voucher for less than what I paid. If this is acceptable for flowers I’d hate to see what’s acceptable for food. While I like the idea they’re going for this is completely unacceptable.

reviews.title: Love the idea but doesn’t work in practice
reviews.text: This is such a wonderful idea and I wish it worked - but the places I would buy from never have any stock. I get way too many notifications and they’re alway for the places I’m not interested in, never actually for the ones I’ve favourited. I always miss out on the ones I want. Uninstalling because the loads of notifications aren’t worth it.

reviews.title: Money gain for multi-million companies
reviews.text: While I did receive a refund of my money spent on the order that was gone upon my arrival (I was late 5 min due to insane unexpected traffic), the customer service had the audacity to blame me for being late (even though it was out of my hands) and hid behind the “rules” while being very rude. May I remind that staff was still in the store cleaning up. Food was already gone even though they could have clearly see the heavy traffic through the window, they decided to allocate food to someone else. Food that I, mom on minimal maternity pay, with 5 month old baby relied on and paid for with money, that means a lot to me at this moment in time. I understand no one has to wait for you when you are late, but a refund should be something people should be entitled to, when the circumstances are out of their hands. Not to mention the time spent on travelling, petrol used to arrive, and at the end I ended up having no food and no money. Luckily they decided to refund me, but overall the experience I have of this concept and the app is - purely money gain for the multimillion companies to be able to sell outdated food to get more money, rather than letting staff to take that food home or giving it away for free to people in need or homeless people. This is business, nothing else that it is advertised for. I am BEYOND disappointed. I will use the voucher and will not use this app ever again! Scam.

reviews.title: Disappointing Business Logic - Defeats the Purpose of Reducing Waste
reviews.text:
I recently used the Too Good To Go app to rescue a Pret bag, but the experience was incredibly frustrating. Due to heavy traffic, I arrived just 5 minutes after the collection window closed. While the Pret staff were very kind and told me I could simply collect the bag tomorrow, the Too Good To Go support staff strictly refused, stating I cannot use my purchased voucher the next day.
This policy feels completely counterintuitive. The core mission of this app is to reduce food waste, yet because of a tiny delay beyond my control, the food I paid for might now go to waste anyway because the app's 'logic' prevents a simple collection the next morning. I don't understand the business logic of charging a customer but then blocking them from actually saving the food. Very disappointed with the lack of flexibility and support.

reviews.title: Not great for those with allergies
reviews.text: EVERYTHING is random. So. Much. Bread. I love hunting down the food that will go to waste and saving it from being thrown out. However, the fact that you have absolutely zero idea of what you’re getting, I can still see a lot of food getting thrown out buy the buyer. It’s just putting money into businesses that plan for these loses anyway. Let alone the more these kinds of apps get out, the more these things will cost the consumer. Just like Woolies and Cole’s don’t mark things as low. Not even on the day of expiry anymore. And so many of my favourite stores are simply selling $10 BOXES now. I live alone. I don’t need twenty of the same thing or only one thing I can eat out of ten. Also. How much of a cut does the app make??

reviews.title: No on-time reminder nor refund options
reviews.text:
After booking, there is an email confirmation about the collection time then that was it. We won’t  get any message or email reminder again among all the busy daily schedules, esp before the collection time closes. If we missed the collection window, then too bad there is no refund options. Not only the food goes wasted, but our money too. And who wins? The company. 
It should have at least give the money back to us. Just like Uber.

reviews.title: No notification for collection and no compensation no recovery for missed orderThe app wastes food
reviews.text: I set up reminder in the app for collection but I haven’t gotten any notification (I checked I have the notification on for the app). And there is no compensation or way of recoup the loss when the collection is missed. The app automatically remove the order to bin and won’t even answer your question. Even more sarcastically, the app display how much food waste you saved under a missed order - and they told you any missed order go automatically to bin (wasted) and no mean of recovery!

reviews.title: TGTG cares more about money and sales than saving food waste
reviews.text: Too Good To Go clearly cares more about selling bags than actually reducing food waste. I received completely unreasonable items (multiple identical cheesecakes, no variety, unreasonable to even eat before spoiling), and when I asked for a refund they refused, even though the order went against the whole point of the app. They talk about “fighting food waste”, but as long as they get the sale, they don’t care what the customer is given or whether the food ends up wasted anyway. Really disappointing experience.
